sources.title: CloudHQ: BIGHOPの全体再開発に関して (Project Asahi Technology Campus), Inzai City Council plenary briefing material of 29 September 2026
sources.publisher: CloudHQ LLC (published by Inzai City as operator-provided council briefing material)
sources.attribution: CloudHQ LLC; published by Inzai City
sources.capture_note: Captured 22 October 2026 (9,464,514 bytes, 37 pages); rehashed against its metadata before use. The deck carries a generic 'strictly confidential' banner, but Inzai City publishes it on its notice page as the operator-provided material presented at the 29 September 2026 council plenary briefing (全員協議会). Only compact factual paraphrase is recorded; the raw file is not redistributed.
sources.summary: CloudHQ's deck on the full redevelopment of BIG HOP Garden Mall Inzai, titled Project Asahi (BIGHOPの全体再開発) Technology Campus. It introduces CloudHQ as a data-centre developer-operator whose first Japanese project is an Osaka joint venture with ESR, describes the mall's flat sales and rising costs, and states that 2025 investor marketing found no demand for a purely commercial redevelopment and interest only from data-centre-based parties. The Gensler site plan (page 31) shows two new 'DC' blocks with office space in the south-centre of the site, retail of 13,345 m2 by Inzai Makinohara Station, a 6,235 m2 community park, an 8,450 m2 non-DC future development plot, a larger future-development plot in the north, and 'EXISTING DCs' in the south-west corner. No capacity, floor area, schedule, permit or start of works is given for the data-centre blocks.
sources.date_semantics: Dated 令和8年9月29日 on every page as Inzai City Council plenary briefing material; published on the city's notice page dated 29 September 2026. Used as the announcement date of the planned data-centre buildings. It is not a permit, consent, land-use decision or construction date.

sources.publisher: Inzai City
sources.capture_note: Captured 22 October 2026 (27,908 bytes); rehashed against its metadata. www.city.inzai.lg.jp serves no robots.txt (HTTP 404), recorded before the first request.
sources.summary: Inzai City reports that, while it revises the district plans of the three Hokuso Line station areas to make data-centre siting (zoning) explicit, the BIG HOP operator explained that it is planning a large-scale redevelopment of the ageing mall and is considering co-locating a data centre on the site and using the proceeds to rebuild the commercial facility. The city set up resident explanation sessions by the operator on 10 and 11 October 2026 and links the operator's material and the city's briefing, both presented at the 29 September 2026 council plenary briefing. The page's FAQ (first appearance not bounded; the page was edited after 29 September) adds that the operator plans two new data-centre buildings after first building the new commercial facilities and plazas, may consider further on-site buildings, targets operation around the mid-2030s with construction timing undecided, and that the plan is at an early stage with no prior consultation or permit procedure with the city.
sources.date_semantics: Page dated [2026年9月29日] (ID 22491). Identity and context for the announcement; the city records the operator's plan and does not approve it.

sources.summary: City-prepared briefing on district-plan changes restricting data centres around the Hokuso Line stations. For the Inzai Makinohara Station front centre district it records that the BIG HOP operator (a landowner) explained a planned large-scale redevelopment and is considering a data centre on the site, and that the city arranged resident sessions in October 2026 outside the normal procedure. Page 16 maps the district on an aerial photograph with the BIG HOP block west of 印西牧の原駅 and a separately boxed '既存DC' (existing data centre) in its south-west corner. The Makinohara-east district change was completed in August 2026; no district-plan decision is recorded for the BIG HOP district.
sources.date_semantics: Dated 令和8年9月29日 (council plenary briefing). Context and identity only; it is not a planning permission or district-plan decision for the BIG HOP site.

sources.publisher: Appomattox County, Virginia (Board of Supervisors; agenda and minutes portal)
sources.title: Appomattox County Board of Supervisors, Special Called Meeting minutes, 31 August 2026 (performance agreement with ADP Appomattox Data Hub, LLC)
sources.summary: At its special called meeting on 31 August 2026 the Board adopted, by roll-call vote 4-1, a resolution approving a performance agreement among Appomattox County, the Appomattox County Economic Development Authority, the Commissioner of the Revenue and ADP Appomattox Data Hub, LLC. The resolution recites that the company 'proposes to develop and operate data center facilities and associated improvements' on Tax Map Parcel 63 A 80, known as the Appomattox Center for Business and Commerce, which is the subject of an option agreement dated 19 April 2024 between the company and the Authority. Grants are payable only from taxes actually collected and subject to appropriation. The resolution states that it does not oblige the Board to approve any rezoning, special or conditional use permit, site plan or other land-use application, and it lapses if the agreement is not executed by 31 December 2026.
sources.date_semantics: The status observation is the Board's adoption of the resolution at the 31 August 2026 meeting. published_at is the portal publication time of these minutes (13 October 2026, from the meeting's publishedFiles record); the PDF's own creation date is 14 September 2026. A performance agreement is an economic-development incentive, not development consent; it supports only an announced project.
sources.personal_data_note: Names of board members and staff in the minutes are not copied.

sources.title: Appomattox County parcel 63 A 80 (Elk Creek; 440.687 assessed acres; owner Economic Development Authority)
sources.summary: The county's public parcel layer (Appomattox_WL_P, layer 12, reached from the county website's GIS Maps link) returns GIS account 63 A 80 three times with identical geometry for its situs addresses 281 Industrial Park Ln, 265 W Ridge Ln and 7561 Richmond Hwy. Owner 'ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY OF', class LOCAL GOVT, 440.687 assessed acres, description Elk Creek. Returned in WGS84, the single-ring polygon (204 vertices) has 453.06 geodesic acres and spans about 2.0 by 1.8 km; its planar centroid (-78.8577799, 37.3723027) lies inside it.

sources.publisher: AVAIO Digital Partners
sources.title: AVAIO Digital: Hercules | Appomattox, Virginia campus page
sources.summary: AVAIO's campus page names Project Hercules at 267 Industrial Park Ln, Appomattox, a 436-acre property, and publishes latitude/longitude 37.374914, -78.848595 (32 m outside the east edge of parcel 63 A 80). It describes the site as construction-ready with site plan approved and fully approved zoning, and expects Dominion power in 2027; it lists 300 MW grid and 700 MW behind-the-meter power (1,000 MW total). The page links its December 2024 announcement.
sources.date_semantics: Undated marketing page; site-plan and zoning claims are not dated and are not used as a status; 2027 power is a forecast. Identity context only.

sources.title: AVAIO Digital to Build $3 Billion Data Center Campus on 452 Acres in Appomattox County, Virginia (10 December 2024)
sources.summary: AVAIO Digital Partners (AVAIO Digital) announced an agreement with the Appomattox County Economic Development Authority to purchase a 452-acre business and industrial site, to be developed as a $3 billion data center campus, and calls the project the Appomattox Data Hub; it reports 300 MW of power confirmed from CVEC and Dominion.
